newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's black political rivals edge together.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's black political rivals edge together.

text.p: Political rivals in South Africa's Zulu province are putting their heads together to make progress in peace efforts, but there is still a long way to go, party officials said on Thursday.

Representatives of Nelson Mandela's African National Congress (ANC) met officials of the Zulu-dominated Inkatha Freedom Party for talks on efforts to end the bitter feuding between their supporters which has killed over 15,000 people since the mid-1980s.
Inkatha chairman Ben Ngubane told reporters after the talks that "innovative ways" were being proposed to end the war.

The ANC has proposed that amnesty be granted to people involved in political violence in KwaZulu-Natal after May 10, 1994 -- the cut-off date for a national amnesty for abuses in the fight over apartheid.
It has also been proposed that Inkatha leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi, home affairs minister in Mandela's national cabinet, be given a more senior position -- perhaps as a deputy president.
Ngubane said the ANC's proposals were under consideration.
"The contribution of the IFP president to stabilise our democracy is certainly on the agenda," he said.
Mandela's party rules at national level, but Inkatha heads the government in KwaZulu-Natal.
Buthelezi and Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, heir-apparent to President Nelson Mandela, are to be briefed on the proposals and the progress in the peace talks next Thursday, officials said.
